title: Nothing derives the documented MCP tool list from createServer, so byte-parity keeps both copies wrong in lockstep
description:
Split out of TASK-204 on its gating reviewer's explicit recommendation, rather than folded in.

**The drift.** The `mcp-server` skill documents a tool count and list that no longer match `createServer`'s actual registrations. As of TASK-204 the server registers **10** tools — `append_comment`, `close_task`, `create_task`, `get_task`, `kb_graph_query`, `kb_lookup`, `list_ready`, `list_todos`, `mcp_build_status`, `transition_status` (verified live against a real spawned child process).

The docs say otherwise, in **three files across two parity trees — six locations**:

- `.claude/skills/mcp-server/references/tool-contract.md:8,189,191` — "the seven task-store tools ... an eighth tool"
- `.claude/skills/mcp-server/references/in-memory-test-harness.md:19` — "all eight tools registered"
- `.claude/skills/mcp-server/SKILL.md:165`
- plus the plugin-root mirrors of all three under `skills/`

**This predates TASK-204.** `in-memory-test-harness.md` has been wrong since TASK-168 added the ninth tool. TASK-204 incremented an existing defect; it did not author it.

**Why the existing sensor does not catch it — this is the actual root cause.** `tests/mcp-server-skill.spec.js` locks byte-parity between the two copies and pins one `list_ready` ground-truth fact. Parity is the wrong invariant here: **it happily keeps both copies wrong together.** Nothing anywhere derives the documented tool list from `createServer`'s real registrations, so the docs can drift arbitrarily far while every sensor stays green.

That is this repo's signature shape — a check that passes without checking the thing that matters (see CLAUDE.md's Empty-result contract, and TASK-184's empty-checked-set class where a doc-lock derived its checked set from a success-only fixture and dutifully verified nothing).

**Why a sensor and not six line edits.** Correcting the prose by hand is the state that already produced this gap twice (TASK-168, then TASK-204). Hand-corrected docs with no sensor will drift again on tool #11. The deliverable here is the mechanism; the prose correction falls out of it.

**Word-boundary matching is required, not optional.** TASK-184 hardened the design-pack doc-lock after a bare substring check made `code` vacuously "documented" via unrelated words like `hardcoded`. Any membership predicate here must not repeat that.
acceptance_criteria: A sensor enumerates the tool names actually registered by createServer (src/mcp-server.js) and asserts each one is documented, failing loudly and naming the missing tool(s) when a tool is added without a doc update. Derive the list from the real registrations - never from a hardcoded copy, which would just relocate the drift.
The membership predicate uses word-boundary matching, not bare substring containment, per TASK-184's hardening of the design-pack doc-lock. State how a near-miss token is rejected.

The sensor is proven non-vacuous: show it failing when a registered tool is removed from the docs, and show its checked set is non-empty and derived from real registrations rather than from a fixture that could be empty.
The reverse direction is decided rather than left implicit: a tool documented but no longer registered. Either assert it too, or state why one-directional coverage is sufficient.

All six drifted locations are corrected to the true tool count and list - three files across .claude/skills/mcp-server/ and their plugin-root mirrors under skills/ - and the parity copies stay byte-identical, verified by hash rather than by eye.

The sensor lives where it actually runs in both npm test and npm run test:all, following the precedent of tests/graph-freshness.spec.js and tests/use-case-policy.spec.js reading repo files directly. Confirm it is selected rather than assuming it.
npm run test:all is green; dist rebuilt and committed if bundled source changes, with dist-parity passing.

comments.author: reviewer
comments.body:
**APPROVE** — final verdict across two rounds. FULL depth, tier `tests-after`. **0 HIGH / 0 MEDIUM / 3 LOW carry-forward.**

Commits `f490378` (sensor + six-location correction) and `3958bfb` (table-row assertion, count removal, `src/` comment).

**Gate:** `test:since -- 3958bfb^` 11 files / 135 passed ⬛ `npm test` 90 files / 1209 passed ⬛ `test:all` **193 passed | 1 skipped (194 files), 2250 passed | 4 skipped, 0 failed**, 98.38s ⬛ `dist-parity` all 8 bundles green, `git status -- dist/` clean ⬛ `check:calibration` clean. Every figure reproduces the developer's report exactly. Parity by direct hash, both trees byte-identical: `tool-contract.md 5724442e…`, `in-memory-test-harness.md 17afe8c3…`, `SKILL.md 5d07f276…`.

## Round 1 — the three highest-risk claims reproduced independently

**Live derivation** — the reviewer instantiated `createServer({repoRoot:'/nonexistent'})` over `InMemoryTransport` itself: `listTools()` returns exactly 10, matching the 10 unconditional `registerTool` calls. **AC1's fast-tier disk claim holds** — every `readFile`/`execFileSync` sits inside a handler or `main()`, and `GRAPH_SCHEMA` is an inline object, not a module-load file read.

**Real pre-fix red** — extracted the six pre-commit doc files via `git show f490378^:<path>` and ran the predicate against the live tool set. Reproduced the developer's claim exactly, identically in both trees.

**AC2 word boundaries** — the reviewer's own near-misses all correctly rejected: `preclose_task_helper`, `close_task_v2`, `xclose_task`, `not_close_task`, `get_tasks`, `target_task`.

**AC4 asymmetry judged honestly reasoned, not a dodge** — `tool-contract.md` has a closed parseable enumeration and the prose files do not, so enforcing reverse there would have meant hardcoding tokens, i.e. relocating the very drift the ticket closes. Its `documented.length > 0` guard is real: deleting the whole table turns the assert red rather than reporting "no phantoms."

## MEDIUM-1 — closed, and the hole was worse than first reported

The reviewer re-ran the row-deletion probe **for all ten tools**, not just the one it originally demonstrated:

```
row-delete append_comment     OLDcheck=[]  NEWcheck=["append_comment"]
row-delete close_task         OLDcheck=[]  NEWcheck=["close_task"]
...
row-delete transition_status  OLDcheck=[]  NEWcheck=["transition_status"]
```

**`OLDcheck=[]` for every single tool.** The anywhere-in-file check stayed green on *all ten* row deletions, because every name is mentioned somewhere outside its own row. The gap was total, not a quirk of `kb_graph_query`, and `findToolsMissingTableRow` closes it for every row.

The spec's two-sided assertion — that the OLD check stays green on the mutated input — is therefore doing real work: it proves the new check closes a gap rather than duplicating `findUndocumentedTools`. The `not.toEqual(realText)` sanity assert is the right guard against the deletion regex silently becoming a no-op.

## MEDIUM-2 — the count surface is eliminated, not relocated

Swept all six doc files plus `src/mcp-server.js` for `\b(seven|eight|eighth|nine|ninth|ten|tenth|eleven)\b`, `tools total`, `registerTool x`, `length 1?[0-9]`. Every total is gone: `ten tools total` ×2, `all ten tools` ×2, `registerTool x10` ×2, `length 10` ×2 — **plus a `three extension tools` count ×3 the developer removed unprompted**, which the reviewer had not named and which would have rotted identically.

`in-memory-test-harness.md:123`'s guidance was rewritten to advise **against** asserting a hardcoded `.length` — turning the doc from a drift source into drift prevention.

Option 2 (stop asserting a count at all, rather than policing the numeral) was the right call: a count is a fact that rots by construction, the itemized list is already authoritative, and a redundant total is a second unsensed surface for the identical defect class.

## MEDIUM-3 — historical-narration distinction ACCEPTED

`src/mcp-server.js:21`'s `TASK-106 (R18) added an EIGHTH tool, kb_lookup` is past-tense, ticket-attributed, and true of the moment it describes; it asserts no present total. It matches established repo convention (`tests/e2e/mcp-server.spec.js:97-102` narrates "an eighth … a ninth … a tenth" the same way, immediately above a live `listTools()` assertion). **Rewriting true history to dodge a numeral would be worse than leaving it.**

**Bundle check confirmed independently:** `git status --short -- dist/` empty and `dist-parity` rebuilds all 8 from *current* `src/` and byte-compares — direct evidence esbuild dropped the amended comment, not an assumption. Consistent with the rule established earlier today: top-of-file and JSDoc comments dropped, interior-position comments preserved. Correct not to commit a `dist/` no-op.

## LOW carry-forward (none blocking)

1. **`the seven task-store tools` remains a hardcoded subgroup count** in six locations (`tool-contract.md:32,203`, `SKILL.md:164`, `in-memory-test-harness.md:19` both trees, `src/mcp-server.js:7`). Same class as the total, on a far more static partition pinned 1:1 to `tasks/schema.json`, so rot rate is near zero — but an eighth ticket-CRUD tool would leave "seven" wrong in six places while the sensor forces its name and row in.
2. **`src/mcp-server.js:6-26`'s SCOPE BOUNDARY enumerates only `kb_lookup`** as the non-CRUD extension, omitting `kb_graph_query` and `mcp_build_status` — a reader concludes the surface is eight tools. The corresponding section in `tool-contract.md:202-214` **was** corrected. Nothing senses this; `tests/mcp-scope-docstring.spec.js:40-70` asserts only keyword presence, never a tool enumeration.
3. Any-context prose matching (open for the two prose-only files) and conditional-registration blindness — both now **recorded in the spec header as accepted limitations** rather than silently assumed away.

**New-test budget:** 15 → 17 (removed the redundant `instanceof` test and its unused import; added 2 per-copy row locks + 1 two-sided non-vacuity proof). All load-bearing. **Tier audit:** `tests-after` correct — the `src/` touch is comment-only, proven by the byte-identical bundle.

**Verdict: APPROVE.** Both MEDIUMs closed at the root rather than papered over, each verified against an independent probe rather than the hand-off's narration.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
**CLOSED on a green independent review after one follow-up round.** Review depth **FULL**; rubric inputs: round 1 was 544 insertions / 52 deletions — over the 150 threshold — AND the diff touches shipped skill docs across two parity trees. Either forces FULL.

Commits `f490378` and `3958bfb`. Tier `tests-after`, audited correct: the `src/mcp-server.js` touch is comment-only, proven by a byte-identical bundle.

## Why this ticket existed

The `mcp-server` skill documented "seven task-store tools ... an eighth tool" and "all eight tools registered" while the server registered **ten**. Wrong since TASK-168 added the ninth; TASK-204 made it two behind.

**The root cause was the interesting part.** `tests/mcp-server-skill.spec.js` locked byte-parity between the two doc copies — and parity is the wrong invariant here, because **it happily keeps both copies wrong together**. Nothing derived the documented list from `createServer`'s real registrations, so the docs could drift arbitrarily far while every sensor stayed green.

That is why this was split out of TASK-204's review rather than folded in: correcting the prose by hand is exactly the state that produced the gap **twice**, and it would have drifted again on tool #11. The deliverable had to be the mechanism.

**The split paid for itself immediately** — the new sensor caught TASK-204's own `mcp_build_status` as undocumented, a ticket written hours earlier flagging a ticket written by a different agent.

## The follow-up round, and why it was worth taking

The reviewer approved round 1 but found two gaps that landed squarely on this ticket's own thesis.

**The forward check didn't require a table row.** Deleting a tool's table row while leaving its prose mention intact kept the sensor green — and that is precisely the sub-defect this ticket had just repaired by hand, since the table was missing rows, not only prose. On re-verification the reviewer found the hole was **total**: it re-ran the row-deletion probe for all ten tools and got `OLDcheck=[]` every time, because every name is mentioned somewhere outside its own row. Not a quirk of one tool — the entire table was unsensed.

The fix's own two-sided assertion is the good part: the spec asserts the **old** check stays green on the mutated input, which is what proves the new check closes a gap rather than duplicating existing coverage.

**The tool COUNT was still unsensed** — rewriting "ten tools total" to "eight tools total" kept everything green. That is literally the string that was wrong in four of the six original locations.

**The developer chose to delete the counts rather than police them**, and that was the better of the two options I offered. Its reasoning: a count is a fact that rots by construction on the next add or remove, the itemized name list is already authoritative, and a redundant total is simply a second unsensed surface for the identical defect class. It also removed a `three extension tools` count the reviewer had never named and which would have rotted identically, and rewrote `in-memory-test-harness.md`'s guidance to advise **against** asserting a hardcoded length — turning a drift source into drift prevention.

**Fixing the generator rather than the output is the distinction that matters here**, and it is what the ticket asked for.

## A judgement call I accepted

`src/mcp-server.js:21`'s `TASK-106 (R18) added an EIGHTH tool` was deliberately left alone. The argument — that it is past-tense, ticket-attributed historical narration rather than a present-tense total — is correct, matches existing repo convention, and **rewriting true history to dodge a numeral would be worse than leaving it.** I asked the reviewer rather than deciding alone; it agreed.

## Verification worth recording

The reviewer reproduced all three high-risk claims under its own probes rather than the hand-off's narration: it instantiated `createServer` itself and got the same 10 tools, extracted the six pre-commit doc files with `git show f490378^:<path>` and reproduced the red exactly, and confirmed the parity hashes directly. It also validated the fast-tier placement claim by checking that every disk read in `src/mcp-server.js` sits inside a handler or `main()`.

The AC4 reverse-direction asymmetry — enforced only against `tool-contract.md`'s parseable table, not the two prose files — was judged **honestly reasoned rather than a dodge**: enforcing it on free-form prose would have required hardcoding tokens, relocating the very drift this ticket closes.

## Carry-forward, non-blocking

- `the seven task-store tools` survives as a hardcoded subgroup count in six locations. Same class, far more static partition (pinned 1:1 to `tasks/schema.json`), so near-zero rot rate — but an eighth CRUD tool would leave "seven" wrong in six places while the sensor forces the new name and row in.
- `src/mcp-server.js:6-26`'s SCOPE BOUNDARY enumerates only `kb_lookup` as the non-CRUD extension, omitting `kb_graph_query` and `mcp_build_status`, so a reader concludes the surface is eight tools. The equivalent section in `tool-contract.md` **was** corrected. Nothing senses it — `tests/mcp-scope-docstring.spec.js` asserts keyword presence only.
- Any-context prose matching (a name in a URL or a `TODO:` line counts as documented) and conditional-registration blindness (`listTools()` cannot see a tool registered only under a non-default option) are now **recorded in the spec header as accepted limitations** rather than silently assumed away.

No `dist/` commit was made or needed — confirmed by a real rebuild-and-compare, not assumed.
